newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Wharf upgraded to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Wharf upgraded to buy.

text.p: Nikko said it had upgraded Wharf Holdings Ltd to a buy from hold and raised its 1996 earnings estimate to HK$3.42 billion from HK$3.21 billion on the assumption of higher development profits.
It said Wharf's prospects for the coming two years, and expectations of annual growth in net profit of 11 to 12 percent for 1997 and 1998, had prompted the rating upgrade.
In a report, Nikko said it expected earnings of about HK$618 million from property sales in the second half of this year.

Wharf has already sold four floors at Telford House for an estimated profit of HK$123 million and the sale of the remaining Telford House floors, together with two floors at Worldwide House, should contribute to the balance, Nikko said.

"It is still an open question as to whether Wharf can extend its uninterrupted run of profit growth to 29 years," Nikko said in the report. But it said with a portfolio of HK$2.3 billion worth of listed shares at the end of 1995, Wharf could produce extra profit. "Also as done before, management could dispose of assets to sister companies for exceptional profits," said Nikko.
Wharf posted first-half net profit of HK$1.30 billion on Wednesday, down from HK$3.00 billion. The shares closed at HK$28.95.
